If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for lagged momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) in last 7 days, apply ±0.25% adjustment to forecast in mid-horizon (8–15 days) based on most recent sentiment direction.
